title: Worship
definition: Worship is the whole-life response of reverence, love, praise, surrender, and obedience to God for who He is and what He has done.
summary: Worship is the whole-life response of reverence, love, praise, surrender, and obedience to God for who He is and what He has done.
christFocus: Jesus is worthy of worship as Lord and Savior, and through Him believers offer their lives to God by the power of the Holy Spirit.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Worship is more than music, emotion, or church style. Scripture presents worship as the whole person responding to God with reverence, gratitude, trust, and obedience.

True worship is shaped by truth. God is worshiped rightly when His people behold His holiness, mercy, glory, justice, and grace as revealed in Scripture and supremely in Christ.

Christ brings believers near to God and makes their worship acceptable. The Holy Spirit forms worship that is not empty performance but sincere surrender.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People can feel excluded from worship because they cannot sing well, stand long, express emotion, or fit a certain church culture. Scripture shows worship is deeper than outward ability; it is a heart and life offered to God through Christ.

This doctrine also corrects consumer worship. The question is not whether worship suited personal preference, but whether God was honored.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Offer your whole life to God as worship. Praise Him with your words, honor Him with your choices, serve Him with your body, and ask the Spirit to make Christ precious to your heart.
